newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI says expects further improvement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI says expects further improvement.

text.p: Heavy engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd said on Tuesday it expected further improvements in the results of its continuing businesses in the second half of the financial year ending June 30.
Harris, noting that the mining sector provided a large segment of ANI's business, said there were signs that uncertainty over aboriginal land claims might delay some major mining projects.
"That would adversely affect some ANI operations," he said.
He said ANI's metals and engineering operations enjoyed significant market share, good geographical coverage and well-recognised brand names.
"These attributes provide an excellent base from which to grow the company into the future," he said.

"These strengths, combined with the implementation of the initiatives highlighted during the strategy review conducted last year, are expected to result in further improvements in the results of ANI's continuing businesses during the second half of 1996/97," Harris said.
He said that over the next six months, management priorities would be:
- further development and implementation of the initiatives identified in last year's strategic review,
- reducing the company's overall exposure to the environmental engineering area,
- developing ANI's major asset, its people
- improving the workplace environment, particularly occupational health and safety,
- further improving working capital management, and
ANI earlier reported a net profit of A$16.33 million for the six months to December 31, up from A$5.19 million a year earlier. Sales rose to A$987.30 million from A$980.07 million.
The company said all its core metals and engineering businesses showed improvement during the period, except for ANI Mineral Processing and the Comsteel division.
